title: Amazon Buying Touch-screen Tech Company
summary: Amazon.com Inc. has acquired Touchco, a New York-based company specializing in touch-screen technology, to enhance its Kindle electronic reader's capabilities. This move positions Amazon to better compete with Apple Inc.'s upcoming iPad. Touchco's technology allows for unlimited and simultaneous touch inputs, offering significant improvements for e-readers.

title: Rentokil's bosses on track for £90m bonus
summary: Rentokil Initial's top executives, Alan Brown, John McAdam, and Andy Ransom, are set to receive £30 million each in bonuses in 2011 following a significant turnaround at the company, particularly its City Link delivery business. The company reported a 54 percent jump in pre-tax profit to £166.5 million in 2009, driven by substantial cost-cutting measures and improved customer service. Despite the financial progress, Rentokil canceled its final dividend for the second consecutive year to strengthen its credit rating and fund future acquisitions.

title: Amazon to pay Microsoft in patent agreement
summary: Microsoft Corp. announced a patent cross-license agreement with Amazon.com Inc., allowing both companies to access each other's technologies. The agreement includes Amazon's Kindle e-reading device and its use of Linux-based servers. Although specific terms are confidential, Amazon.com will pay an undisclosed amount to Microsoft as part of the deal.

title: Nintendo unveils DSi XL video-game player that includes e-reader, competes with Apple, Amazon.com
summary: Nintendo announced the release of its new DSi XL handheld video-game player in the U.S., which will include an e-reader function to compete with products from Apple and Amazon.com. The device, featuring a larger screen, will be released on March 28 and cost $189.99, alongside a "100 Classic Books" title in June. This move comes as Nintendo faces increasing competition from Apple in the mobile gaming market.
